title: Keystroke Dynamics Patterns While Writing Positive and Negative Opinions
abstract: This paper analyzes behavioral patterns in human-computer interaction by examining keystroke dynamics while participants wrote positive and negative opinions. A semi-experiment with 50 participants revealed that keystroke patterns could differentiate opinions with accuracy above random guess, though combining with other modalities may improve results.
problem_statement: Differentiating positive and negative opinions based on keystroke dynamics patterns during text input.
methodology: Semi-experimental study with 50 participants writing opinions on learning experiences. Keystroke dynamics were captured and over 50 features analyzed for classification accuracy.
dataset: Keystroke data from 50 participants writing opinions on positive/negative learning experiences and teacher interactions.
evaluation_metrics: Self-report labels of pleasure and arousal
performance: Classification accuracy slightly above random guess; second approach using self-report labels achieved more accurate results.
contribution: Demonstrated feasibility of recognizing positive/negative opinions from keystroke patterns with accuracy above random guess.
limitations: Accuracy could be improved by combining keystroke data with other modalities.
future_work: Explore multimodal approaches integrating keystroke dynamics with physiological or contextual data.

title: Under Pressure: Sensing Stress of Computer Users
abstract: Recognizing when computer users are stressed can help reduce their frustration and prevent negative health conditions. This work explores using a pressure-sensitive keyboard and capacitive mouse to discriminate between stressful and relaxed conditions in a laboratory study.
problem_statement: Measuring stress non-invasively and continuously at work remains an open challenge.
methodology: A within-subjects laboratory study using a pressure-sensitive keyboard and capacitive mouse to detect behavioral changes during stressful tasks.
dataset: 24 participants performing expressive writing, text transcription, and mouse clicking tasks over 30 minutes.
performance: 79% of participants showed increased typing pressure; 75% showed more mouse surface contact during stressful conditions.
contribution: Demonstrates the feasibility of using keyboard and mouse interactions to sense stress in computer users.
limitations: Results are limited to a lab setting and may not generalize to real-world scenarios.
future_work: Explore real-world applications and integrate stress sensing into adaptive systems.

title: The Effect of Emotion on Keystroke: An Experimental Study Using Facial Feedback Hypothesis
abstract: Automatic emotion recognition technology is explored through keystroke dynamics under facial feedback-induced emotional states. A controlled experiment validated significant differences in typing patterns between positive and negative emotions.
problem_statement: Limited empirical studies on emotion's effect on keystroke patterns. Existing methods are intrusive or require specialized equipment.
methodology: Facial feedback hypothesis used to induce emotions via teeth/lip conditions. Keystroke duration and latency analyzed using t-tests on 15 participants' typing data.
dataset: 15 university students (mean age 23.4) typed number sequence '67829751' under positive (teeth) and negative (lip) emotional states.
evaluation_metrics: Independent samples t-tests on keystroke features
performance: Significant differences in keystroke duration/latency between emotional states (p < 0.05). High accuracy in distinguishing positive/negative states.
contribution: Validated emotion-keystroke correlation through controlled experiments, supporting non-intrusive emotion recognition via typing patterns.
limitations: Small sample size (15 participants) and limited emotional induction methods (facial feedback only).
future_work: Expand to diverse emotional states, integrate multimodal data, and improve generalizability across populations.

abstract: Emotion can be measured/recognized from physiological and behavioral responses. This paper reviews state-of-the-art emotion recognition methods from keystroke, mouse, and touchscreen dynamics, addressing challenges and future directions for non-intrusive emotion detection.
problem_statement: The primary challenge is accurately and easily recognizing emotional states from non-intrusive secondary data like keystroke, mouse, and touchscreen dynamics.
methodology: Systematic literature review of 102 papers focusing on emotion elicitation methods, recognition features, and classification techniques.
performance: Studies show varying accuracy (60-95%) depending on emotion type, feature extraction, and classification methods.
contribution: Provides systematic review of KMT dynamics-based emotion recognition, answers six research questions, and identifies key gaps and future directions.
limitations: Limited focus on real-world applications and long-term emotional state tracking.
future_work: Developing robust models for diverse contexts, integrating multimodal data, and improving generalizability across populations.

title: Identify user features impacting keystroke, mouse and touchscreen dynamics
abstract: To understand how individual user features affect one’s emotional changes in response to stimuli or changes in a situated external environment, it is necessary to measure how user features affect behavioral changes in the use of keyboard, mouse, and touchscreen devices (KMT dynamics).
problem_statement: Understanding how user features influence KMT dynamics and emotional states, and developing a framework for personalized emotion recognition.
methodology: Conducted a questionnaire survey with 107 participants and data analysis to explore relationships between user features and KMT dynamics features.
contribution: Identified key user features (gender, proficiency, etc.) and KMT dynamics features; proposed a new personalized emotion recognition framework.
limitations: Initial framework focuses only on KMT dynamics; integration of user features into behavioral features remains unclear.
future_work: Refine framework based on findings; explore additional user features like cultural context and emotional states.
